It's bad for everything now, but vertical integration makes it worse. The OEM model allows multiple manufacturers to gear up to build parts, they all then need to be fully interchangeable for a whole known model run. This gives a lot more access for third party manufacture of parts. Tesla and the Chinese manufacturers all focus on vertical integration, there are less companies that can build any one part. They have better control of the pricing of the part, and there is generally less supply and supply channels. It's just bad for consumers in general. The other issue is incompatibility of parts/subsystems. Under the OEM model you could buy the same part from 6 manufacturers and be guaranteed it would work. Now you might have 3 version of a reverse parking sensor but none are interchangeable. You can't order parts until you pull the old one and inspect it. This isn't a Chinese manufacturing problem as much as it is a manufacturing without caring about maintenance and repair/disposable cars. Tesla are worse than the Chinese in this regard, they just have, actually had, a bigger market share so it was less noticeable.
